items.summary: Derived data and analysis artifacts accompanying Structural memory links experimental discovery and computational novelty . Author note: D. Nguyen and K. Cao contributed equally to this work. The analysis embeds 167,392 ICSD entries with CrystalWeave, follows structural neighborhoods through publication time, and compares public cohorts from GNoME, MatterGen, Materials Project theoretical-only, JARVIS-DFT and Alexandria-PBE. Alternative representations are Magpie-22, Graphlet (CrystalNN), Graphlet (VoronoiNN), and AMD-100. The artifacts cover historical densification and research renaissances, external-cohort basin occupancy, scale-invariant formula precedent, and synthesis-outcome comparisons using A-Lab and the Kononova collection. Corrections: Feature-dependent analyses were regenerated after corrections to elemental-species and disordered-site handling, periodic neighbors and graph construction, Graphlet encoding, and AMD basin eligibility. Candidate-structure figures preserve the source fractional coordinates and distinguish candidate symmetry from community statistics. Earlier feature matrices, assignments and numerical results must not be mixed with this release. Files: Sixteen individually downloadable files: four compressed feature archives, a derived-analysis archive split into eight numbered parts, an exact public-repository source snapshot, README, release manifest and SHA-256 checksums. Join the eight analysis parts as described in the README before extraction. The archives use tar plus Zstandard compression (.tar.zst). The analysis archive includes AMD-100 features, fitted projection states, assignments, numerical controls, corrected candidate figures, and the 57 public pre-experiment A-Lab targets with provenance. Its current-results guide identifies superseded AMD and Magpie diagnostics. Raw Magpie-22 descriptors (~6 GB) are omitted; partition PCA coordinates, current common-transform scoring coordinates and fitted state are supplied. Source coverage: The source snapshot includes the recovered nearest-ICSD Element Mover's Distance, disorder-aware structure-matching and ICSD partial-occupancy extraction producers, their maintained entry points, numerical tests and dependency documentation. Their saved outputs and scientific recovery provenance are supplied in the analysis archive. Licensed ICSD source CIFs and the raw ICSD source index are excluded. Recomputing analyses that read those inputs requires an appropriate ICSD license. Selected external structures retain their documented public-source provenance. The accompanying public code repository is scattering/crystal-communities-paper . The source archive is exported directly from public commit 0f4ae1ae788800d93d1beacf2d8529e7bcca641b . The release manifest records the source commit and archive checksums. Dataset license: CC BY 4.0; source code and third-party components retain their accompanying license notices.
items.title: Derived data and analysis artifacts for: Structural memory links experimental discovery and computational novelty

items.summary: Phase-field trajectories governed by the Allen--Cahn equation determine the effective force $G=F'/\eps^2$, but not the free-energy potential $F$ and interfacial scale $\eps$ separately. We introduce surface-tension-calibrated Allen--Cahn identification (STAC), a two-step method that resolves this ambiguity using an independently supplied surface tension. First, space--time weak moments produce a linear inverse problem without differentiating the measured field. A Bernstein representation with positive coefficients enforces two stable pure phases and a single central energy maximum. Second, the surface tension fixes the remaining scale algebraically. We prove scale equivalence of the forward model, uniqueness of the calibrated pair within this class, and finite perturbation bounds that remain valid when the potential vanishes at the pure phases. Experiments with resolved synthetic phase fields separate the effects of the structural constraint, ridge regularization, and constitutive approximation error. Across 80 shared noisy records, unconstrained degree-five regression produces six potentials with an incorrect well structure. Positivity combined with ridge regularization eliminates these violations and reduces the mean force error from 8.70\% to 5.66\%. Lower-degree models are nevertheless more accurate in some tests, and an admissible law outside the positive Bernstein family shows how the constraint can introduce approximation bias. STAC thus recovers a structurally admissible, physically scaled potential while making explicit which information comes from the observed dynamics and which comes from the independent surface-tension datum.
items.title: Constrained weak identification of Allen--Cahn free energies with surface-tension calibration

items.summary: We present a physics-informed machine learning framework based on Neural Ordinary Differential Equations that solves the holographic inverse problem: reconstructing the bulk spacetime and gauge field of a charged AdS black hole directly from boundary fermionic spectral functions. Encoding the UV asymptotics, horizon regularity, and zero temperature extremality as hard constraints in the neural network architecture, our framework reliably reconstructs the extremal Reissner-Nordström AdS geometry across three quantum critical regimes set by the $U(1)$ probe charge---non-Fermi liquid, marginal Fermi liquid (strange metal), and Fermi-liquid-like states---and can jointly infer the probe charge itself to sub-percent accuracy. Relaxing the near-AdS boundary constraint uncovers a geometrical degeneracy: bulk profiles that differ throughout the radial direction but share the same near-horizon $AdS_2 \times \mathbb{R}^2$ data reproduce identical spectral functions near the Fermi surface. This isospectral non-uniqueness is precisely the bulk degeneracy expected on general holographic grounds at zero temperature, and its spontaneous emergence across independent training runs shows that the network isolates the IR CFT universality rather than overfitting a single UV completion.
items.title: Deep learning emergent spacetime from fermionic spectral functions in holography

items.summary: Analysis code, derived result tables, figures and the pre-specified analysis plan for a study of direction-consistent differential gene expression between non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (GSE89632, GSE126848) and bladder urothelial carcinoma (TCGA-BLCA). Contains the complete pipeline in Python, the output and provenance record of every stage, the full direction-consistent gene table and enrichment table untruncated, and the analysis plan with its thresholds fixed before any data were examined together with the amendments made afterwards. Raw input data is not included: all three datasets are public and are better obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus and the NCI Genomic Data Commons. The provenance files record exactly which files were retrieved, when, and with what checksums. The five folders are uploaded as one zip archive each because the repository accepts at most 100 files per record. README.md and MANIFEST.tsv are left unpacked.
items.title: NAFLD and bladder urothelial carcinoma transcriptome overlap: analysis code and derived results

items.summary: Conformance vectors for agent execution evidence, and the reference verifier that judges them. The suite carries eight corpora: the in-toto adversarial-execution-evidence predicate, the in-toto ai-agent-action predicate, SCITT COSE carriage, an anchor-stream verifier, ACS core, an artifact-binding contract, a cross-run record contract, and ACI deployments. One binary judges every one of them, selected by the suite each corpus manifest declares. The predicate's model is execute-and-attest rather than match-and-assert: a consumer recomputes the outcome from the bytes the statement carries, instead of trusting a verdict the producer asserted about itself. This repository is a second, independently usable implementation of that contract, so that any producer of the predicate type can self-certify and any consumer can reject a lying emitter. This deposit covers suite revision 28 of the corpus: 272 vectors, of which 61 accept, 209 reject and 2 are indeterminate, exercised by rails in two languages. The bytes are fixed by the corpus digest 8b035678def9e5ac00ba761b8c640e4412c57163134afb9d2c1a90f49d573a52 recorded in vectors/MANIFEST.json, which tells this deposit from any other revision without anyone recounting it. The corpus is versioned and immutable per revision. A published revision is never mutated in place; a normative change to the predicate, or an addition to the corpus, bumps the revision and regenerates every vector byte-identically from its generators, because the vendored specification's digest is itself a corpus input. The intended use is citation by a conformance requirement. A requirement that names this suite, or any other suite demonstrated to exercise the same conditions, is checkable by a party who trusts neither the producer nor the implementer.
items.title: agent-evidence-vectors: conformance vectors for agent execution evidence

items.summary: Supplementary data and code accompanying the manuscript “An Evidence-Chain Provenance Framework for Tracing the Overseas Circulation of Oracle Bones: A GIS-Based Approach” (Humanities and Social Sciences Communications; Manuscript ID eaed1ecb-153b-4b2f-99cf-8bca05b564b3). This package provides materials for editors and referees to check the study’s methods and results. It includes: (i) the Tier A–D evidence-classification coding scheme; (ii) circulation-pathway tables and CSV files aligned with Tables 1–3; (iii) record-level evidence codes underlying Fig. 6; (iv) an English evidence-ledger digest; (v) a bilingual Chinese–English concordance of cited Chinese-language sources and personal names; (vi) location notes for GIS visualizations; (vii) Python scripts used to generate Figs. 1–6; (viii) finished figure PNGs matching the manuscript; and (ix) a public-domain Natural Earth basemap for re-running Fig. 5. The study synthesizes published historical sources, museum catalogues, and publicly disclosed institutional records. No new laboratory, survey, or interview datasets were generated. Author-generated materials are shared under CC BY 4.0; copyrighted verbatim text of published sources is cited but not reproduced in full. Natural Earth data are public domain.
items.title: Supplementary for "An Evidence-Chain Provenance Framework for Tracing the Overseas Circulation of Oracle Bones: A GIS-Based Approach"

items.summary: This deposit contains the data, code, and figures underlying a study of owned dog and cat populations in Ecuador, reconstructed from the 2022 Population and Housing Census (Censo de Población y Vivienda, CPV 2022) of the National Institute of Statistics and Censuses (INEC). It includes: (i) indicator tables of dog and cat ownership at the province, canton, and parish levels (CSV), with derived indicators such as the percentage of households keeping pets, pets per capita, and the dog-to-cat ratio; (ii) geospatial layers (GeoPackage) joining these indicators to canton and parish boundaries, plus the local spatial-cluster (LISA) classification; (iii) the full analysis pipeline (Python) that builds the indicators from the primary census tabulations, harmonizes place names and geometries, runs the spatial analysis, and generates the figures; (iv) the five manuscript figures (TIFF, 300 dpi); and (v) a documented log of figures on companion-animal populations circulated in Ecuadorian media and official communications, compared with the values reconstructed here. At the national level, the census records 7,601,269 owned dogs and cats (5,211,037 dogs and 2,390,232 cats), with 58.3% of households keeping at least one. Ownership is markedly higher in rural areas and strongly clustered across the central-southern Sierra (global Moran's I = 0.57). Raw inputs are not all redistributed here for licensing reasons; see the README and SOURCES file for provenance, licensing, and instructions to reproduce the analysis. Code is released under the MIT License and derived data under CC BY 4.0.
items.title: Household dog and cat populations in Ecuador from the 2022 census: indicator datasets, spatial analysis, and figures

items.summary: Reproducibility deposit for ProteoAnalyst, an integrated web platform for downstream proteomics and phosphoproteomics analysis (proteoanalyst.ca). Every value in the paper's benchmark and validation tables is regenerated by the scripts included here. Each file is independently downloadable; README.md is the entry point and DEPOSIT_MANIFEST.tsv lists every file with its SHA-256. Contents Analysis backend • ProteoAnalystR_1.0.0.tar.gz — the R backend under review (source package; also at   github.com/xia-lab/ProteoAnalystR), with its build commit and SHA-256. Benchmarks (public controlled-mixture ground truth; each bundle self-contained and self-scoring) • DDA / MaxQuant — iPRG-2015 (MassIVE RMSV000000249.2; SI Table S5a): three differential-   expression engine arms (limma, DEqMS, msqrob2) scored head-to-head against the published   MSstats reference, plus the missing-value robustness sweep (Table S7) and a reproducible   DE-runtime sweep (Table S10); and a second, independent DDA spike-in on DEqMS's own MaxLFQ   two-proteome example (PRIDE PXD000279; Table S5b). • DIA / Spectronaut — LFQbench HYE124 (Table S6a): the shipped msqrob2 default vs limma and   DEqMS arms, scored against species-defined truth and the MSstats reference; and a second,   independent DIA spike-in on the UPS1 example dataset (ExperimentHub EH7782; MassIVE   MSV000087597; Table S6b). • MSstatsPTM simulations (Table S8) and the Hogrebe two-species phospho spike-in (PRIDE   PXD007145; Table S9) — protein-adjusted PTM and site-level phospho accuracy vs MSstatsPTM,   including a native MSstatsPTM package arm. • A provenance/reports bundle (fetch scripts, checksums, and   the manuscript-cited scoring report). • Two method-validation bundles: semi-synthetic PTM-occupancy / isoform-usage mixtures (Tables   S11 and S13), and an orthogonal transcript (DM1) validation of the isoform-usage detector   (Table S12). Case studies (reproduce end-to-end from the download) • CS1 palmitate islets; CS2 FB231 mitophagy; CS3 phospho / TKI resistance (PRIDE PXD005536);   CS4 isoform-usage + PTM occupancy. Each carries its inputs, bundled annotation, recorded command   history, expected results, and sessionInfo.txt. Data availability: the benchmark inputs derive from public MassIVE/PRIDE deposits; CS3 is PRIDE PXD005536; CS1 is ethics-approved, de-identified human and stem-cell-derived islet proteomics generated by the James Johnson lab (University of British Columbia); CS2 and CS4 were generated by the Jean-François Trempe lab (McGill University).
items.title: ProteoAnalyst: benchmarks and case-study

items.summary: SynInsight Atlas is a literature-derived synthesis pathway dataset for developing and evaluating machine-learning retrosynthesis models. It contains 6,555 reaction-step occurrences across 635 recorded paths from 91 publications , representing 2,166 distinct operations. The dataset is provided in CSV format, with molecular structures, reaction conditions, route connectivity, source references, and curation status. Field definitions, provenance records, and file checksums support reproducible reuse. This is a candidate release pending independent chemical review . Paths include partial syntheses, fragment preparations, and control branches; shared operations may occur in multiple paths. No fixed evaluation split or starting-material stock is supplied. Data and annotations are released under CC BY 4.0 . Original publications and supporting-information files are not included.
items.title: SynInsight Atlas: Literature-Derived Synthesis Pathways for Retrosynthesis Benchmarking

items.summary: Replication materials for a methods paper documenting twenty-three measured defects in GDELT as a research instrument, and for a companion findings paper on narrative crisis detection across six Nigerian cases, 2014-2024. Contains: the retrieval and analysis package; a provenance database of 4,943 logged retrievals (endpoint, parameters, response SHA-256, outcome); pre-registration documents for all three rounds; case specification files; re-executable boundary probes with a recorded run; and the thirteen-step validation protocol as a runnable checker. Raw GDELT records are deliberately excluded. The provenance database records the exact request behind every figure so that each can be re-executed against GDELT directly.
items.title: Silent Failure Modes in GDELT-Based Crisis Research: replication materials

items.summary: Large language model agents tune GPU kernels and serving engines through a closed loop of propose, measure, and keep, but the measurements behind this loop are not trustworthy. We characterize four failure modes from a four-day pilot corpus of 619 model calls: strawman baselines manufacture speedups, absolute times do not transfer across machines, saturated tasks nullify comparisons, and infrastructure defects impersonate science. We present AutoTuneBench, a benchmark and measurement protocol that makes trust architectural. The protocol is frozen as code with test-enforced provenance; a database-level validator rejects out-of-protocol results; anti-cheat checks run outside the agent's modification surface; comparisons follow pre-registered readouts; and measurements anchor to externally published results, grounded in paired-seed statistics with a 5\% cross-run coefficient-of-variation cap. Honest measurement rewrites the headlines: our best kernel reads 10.6x against a naive baseline but 2.03x against the honest one; one configuration delivers 1.174x on one machine and 1.0049x on another; a pre-registered on/off comparison nulls at a shared wall (2.4840 vs 2.4957\,ms); and the KernelBench Level-1 suite admits 51\% of tasks with median speedup 1.0001x over PyTorch eager. The protocol, the two-engine corpus (vLLM and SGLang), and its audit trail are released as open artifacts.
items.title: AutoTuneBench: Trustworthy Measurement for Agent Auto-Tuning of LLM Serving Engines

items.summary: This dataset contains 93 manually selected RELION 2D class averages generated from particle images in the EMPIAR-12036 entry of the Electron Microscopy Public Image Archive. The underlying molecule has D3 symmetry. The authors initially generated a set of class averages using RELION and manually selected 93 classes after discarding those that were visually uninterpretable. Each selected image is 320 by 320 pixels. These images were used as an experimental dataset for evaluating symmetric non-unique games (NUG) orientation estimation in the unpublished manuscript cited below. The MRC file contains a single image stack with shape (93, 320, 320). The first axis indexes class averages, and the remaining axes are image coordinates. This curated subset supports reproduction of the NUG orientation-estimation and ab initio reconstruction stages. It does not reproduce the preceding RELION classification or manual class-selection stages. Manuscript: Shi, Y., Singer, A., Wang, J., and Yang, R. (2026). Orientation Estimation of Cryo-EM Images for Molecules with Arbitrary Symmetry by Semidefinite Programming. Unpublished manuscript. Source dataset: EMPIAR-12036, Electron Microscopy Public Image Archive. https://doi.org/10.6019/EMPIAR-12036
items.title: EMPIAR-12036 Class Averages for D3 Symmetric NUG Orientation Estimation

items.summary: It has been over fifty years since Kenneth Wilson had his Nobel-prize-winning ideas on the renormalization group. In this time frame, despite many attempts, no mathematical results have implemented Wilson's vision to a satisfactory degree. Although a number of predictions stemming from the renormalization group framework have been proven to date, these proofs usually rely on alternative ideas and do not cover the full predictive power of Wilson's renormalization group. The discovery of pathologies within rigorous implementations of renormalization group transformations have further reduced the enthusiasm of the mathematics community for this subject. This paper presents a novel framework to implement Wilson's original idea in a rigorous manner based on inverse limits of finite systems. Doing so, one avoids these pathologies and hence obtains a mathematically sound framework for Wilson's renormalization group. This opens up a completely new path to tackle some of the existing problems in rigorous renormalization group theory like the existence of non-trivial fixed points.
items.title: Pathology-Free Real-Space Renormalization Group Theory on an Inverse Limit Space

items.summary: Capable open-weight models make local coding and reasoning attractive, but their context and execution state strain laptop memory. We present JustFit, an MLX-based inference runtime that combines KVExec for compressed KV execution, PhaseSwap for component residency, and StateTrans for state-preserving serving transitions. These mechanisms fuse reconstruction and coordinate just-in-time materialization and release, independently of model-weight quantization. In full-execution capacity tests on a 24 GiB M4 Pro MacBook running Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4, three independent runs complete 196,608 input and 16,384 output tokens, increasing completed single-request context from the mlx-vlm baseline's 30,720 positions to 212,992 (6.93x); a separate two-request run retains 229,376 positions in aggregate. In separate performance tests, a 32K-input, 64-output probe reaches 19.11 tokens/s, and a repeated 32K+6K workload has a median peak process footprint of 16,374 MiB. The integrated runtime answers 29 of 30 AIME 2026 problems correctly, showing how compact state and lifetime-aware execution expand local serving capacity while supporting extended generated reasoning.
items.title: JustFit: 200K-Token LLM Serving on a 24 GiB Laptop with Just-in-Time State Management

items.summary: Classical dynamic programming represents optimal sequential decisions through value functions and policies. While this functional representation is natural for computing optimal decisions, it does not directly identify the mathematical object governing policy reconstruction, representation complexity, or oracle-query complexity once an optimal policy is fixed. This paper addresses this question by developing a geometric theory of structured optimal policies in which the decision-boundary geometry induced by the policy becomes the primary object of analysis. We show that, under suitable structural regularity conditions, this geometry provides the minimal representation required for policy reconstruction and determines the statistical and computational complexity of the reconstruction problem. Building upon this representation, we establish structural properties of policy-induced decision geometry, introduce intrinsic notions of boundary and decision complexity, derive information-theoretic measures of decision compression, and obtain statistical guarantees for boundary estimation and policy reconstruction from black-box policy queries. Collectively, these results demonstrate that, for the structured decision problems considered here, the complexity of policy reconstruction is governed by the geometry of the decision boundary rather than by the cardinality of the ambient state space. Controlled numerical experiments examine the principal theoretical predictions and provide empirical evidence consistent with the proposed framework.
items.title: A Geometric Theory of Decision Boundaries in Structured Markov Decision Processes

items.summary: A3P5 NEMESIS is a four-wheel rover intended to combine remote inspection, environmental observation and lightweight manipulation within one serviceable platform. This study develops a photo-constrained geometric reconstruction, a subsystem architecture and a reproducible analytical assessment while distinguishing physical prototype evidence from proposed functions. An exploratory search retrieved 5,000 bibliographic records across ten queries, yielding 4,897 distinct DOI records and 1,212 metadata candidates; selected primary studies and technical documents informed the design. The reconstructed configuration retains the carbon-pattern enclosure, independently steered wheel assemblies, folded manipulator, inclined camera mast and side sampling equipment. A declared 24 kg scenario predicts 3.28 newton-metres of gearbox-output torque per wheel on a 20-degree grade under equal load sharing; a separate static model shows how a 2 kg forward payload reduces the geometric front-tipping bound from 38.1 degrees to 32.7 degrees. These are design screens, not measured operating limits. A public-data calibration benchmark uses 7,344 eligible hourly observations, eight sensor/environmental predictors and chronological training, validation and test partitions. Validation-selected ridge regression achieves a held-out CO root-mean-square error of 0.502 milligrams per cubic metre, with a 95% daily-block bootstrap interval of 0.435-0.569 milligrams per cubic metre. This result concerns an external sensor array and cannot establish NEMESIS accuracy. The combined analysis identifies priority measurements, proposed control interfaces and mission-specific validation requirements. The contribution is a traceable engineering design study and evaluation framework for a prototype whose integrated field performance remains to be established.
items.title: A3P5 NEMESIS Integrated Rover Design for Environmental Reconnaissance and Robotic Sampling with Reproducible Mobility Analysis and an External Data Machine Learning Calibration Benchmark

items.summary: Supplementary data and code accompanying the manuscript “An Evidence-Chain Provenance Framework for Tracing the Overseas Circulation of Oracle Bones: A GIS-Based Approach” (Humanities and Social Sciences Communications; Manuscript ID eaed1ecb-153b-4b2f-99cf-8bca05b564b3). This package provides materials for editors and referees to check the study’s methods and results. It includes: (i) the Tier A–D evidence-classification coding scheme; (ii) circulation-pathway tables and CSV files aligned with Tables 1–3; (iii) record-level evidence codes underlying Fig. 6; (iv) an English evidence-ledger digest; (v) a bilingual Chinese–English concordance of cited Chinese-language sources and personal names; (vi) location notes for GIS visualizations; (vii) Python scripts used to generate Figs. 1–6; (viii) finished figure PNGs matching the manuscript; and (ix) a public-domain Natural Earth basemap for re-running Fig. 5. The study synthesizes published historical sources, museum catalogues, and publicly disclosed institutional records. No new laboratory, survey, or interview datasets were generated. Author-generated materials are shared under CC BY 4.0; copyrighted verbatim text of published sources is cited but not reproduced in full. Natural Earth data are public domain.
items.title: Supplementary for "An Evidence-Chain Provenance Framework for Tracing the Overseas Circulation of Oracle Bones: A GIS-Based Approach"

items.summary: FastWAM-style world action models enable efficient action-only inference, but generalize poorly under visual distribution shifts. Their reconstruction-oriented representations emphasize appearance-specific details, limiting generalization to unseen scenes and objects. Without observation history, the model also lacks temporal evidence for robustly identifying task-relevant state changes and motion in unfamiliar visual conditions. To address these limitations, we present the Causal Semantic World Action Model (CSWAM), which augments FastWAM with a causal semantic expert built on V-JEPA 2.1. V-JEPA provides temporally grounded representations of semantic state changes and motion with less dependence on appearance-specific details. The expert learns their future evolution from a sparse history of current and past observations and shares the history-derived context with both the video and action streams through causal attention. At inference, CSWAM conditions action denoising on the current video state and observed semantic history, retaining efficient action-only inference. We conduct simulation and real-robot experiments to evaluate generalization under distribution shifts. With embodied pretraining, CSWAM raises Randomized success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean-to-Randomized transfer from 10.16% to 45.18%, a gain of 35.02 percentage points over FastWAM. Across two real-robot tasks and three OOD difficulty levels, CSWAM improves average success over FastWAM by 42.5 percentage points, from 27.5% to 70.0%.
items.title: CSWAM: Better Causal Semantic Representations for Out-of-Distribution Generalization in World Action Models

items.summary: Long-term memory is becoming a core substrate for personalized AI, yet most systems still represent personalization as discrete records in a largely static latent space, accessed under one global similarity notion. For data mining, this creates a mismatch: the evidence is a temporal event stream, while the dominant abstraction is a searchable record set. We argue that long-horizon personalization should instead model memory as a user-specific dynamical state space with locally heterogeneous geometry. Geometry here is a computational language, not a literal claim about cognition: it captures stable versus volatile regions, variable-rate drift, heterogeneous neighborhoods, and uncertainty about current user state. Profiles and isolated events remain useful as points, but interaction, feedback, and elapsed time induce trajectories. Memory access then becomes trajectory-conditioned reconstruction of the relevant user state, not only nearest-neighbor lookup.
items.title: Memory Has Geometry: Non-Uniform Geometric Memory for Long-Horizon Personalized AI

items.summary: Replication materials for a methods paper documenting twenty-three measured defects in GDELT as a research instrument, and for a companion findings paper on narrative crisis detection across six Nigerian cases, 2014-2024. Contains: the retrieval and analysis package; a provenance database of 4,943 logged retrievals (endpoint, parameters, response SHA-256, outcome); pre-registration documents for all three rounds; case specification files; re-executable boundary probes with a recorded run; and the thirteen-step validation protocol as a runnable checker. Raw GDELT records are deliberately excluded. The provenance database records the exact request behind every figure so that each can be re-executed against GDELT directly.
items.title: Silent Failure Modes in GDELT-Based Crisis Research: replication materials

items.summary: Large language model agents tune GPU kernels and serving engines through a closed loop of propose, measure, and keep, but the measurements behind this loop are not trustworthy. We characterize four failure modes from a four-day pilot corpus of 619 model calls: strawman baselines manufacture speedups, absolute times do not transfer across machines, saturated tasks nullify comparisons, and infrastructure defects impersonate science. We present AutoTuneBench, a benchmark and measurement protocol that makes trust architectural. The protocol is frozen as code with test-enforced provenance; a database-level validator rejects out-of-protocol results; anti-cheat checks run outside the agent's modification surface; comparisons follow pre-registered readouts; and measurements anchor to externally published results, grounded in paired-seed statistics with a 5\% cross-run coefficient-of-variation cap. Honest measurement rewrites the headlines: our best kernel reads 10.6x against a naive baseline but 2.03x against the honest one; one configuration delivers 1.174x on one machine and 1.0049x on another; a pre-registered on/off comparison nulls at a shared wall (2.4840 vs 2.4957\,ms); and the KernelBench Level-1 suite admits 51\% of tasks with median speedup 1.0001x over PyTorch eager. The protocol, the two-engine corpus (vLLM and SGLang), and its audit trail are released as open artifacts.
items.title: AutoTuneBench: Trustworthy Measurement for Agent Auto-Tuning of LLM Serving Engines

items.summary: Analysis code, derived result tables, figures and the pre-specified analysis plan for a study of direction-consistent differential gene expression between non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (GSE89632, GSE126848) and bladder urothelial carcinoma (TCGA-BLCA). Contains the complete pipeline in Python, the output and provenance record of every stage, the full direction-consistent gene table and enrichment table untruncated, and the analysis plan with its thresholds fixed before any data were examined together with the amendments made afterwards. Raw input data is not included: all three datasets are public and are better obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus and the NCI Genomic Data Commons. The provenance files record exactly which files were retrieved, when, and with what checksums. The five folders are uploaded as one zip archive each because the repository accepts at most 100 files per record. README.md and MANIFEST.tsv are left unpacked.
items.title: NAFLD and bladder urothelial carcinoma transcriptome overlap: analysis code and derived results

items.summary: Small differences on coding-agent leaderboards are often read as an ordering of systems. We audit whether the published verdicts support this reading, using 254 SWE-bench submissions across four splits without running models. On Verified, the leading two entries each resolve 396 of 500 instances. The top ten share 285 successes and 51 failures, leaving 164 instances that distinguish their outcomes. Frontier solution sets have median nesting 0.935 against a score-implied baseline of 0.774, indicating strongly shared successes. Scores also depend on the evaluated model-scaffold pair: observed within-model scaffold ranges reach 29.8 percentage points, compared with the 8.8-point spread of the top thirty. Six of nine cell-mean interaction tests remain significant after Holm correction, although this observational design does not identify causal scaffold effects. Exact paired McNemar tests separate none of the 29 adjacent Verified top-thirty pairs at alpha=0.05, while the larger Test split separates 14 of 23. A stated leader-based rule yields three descriptive tiers, or two after Holm correction; non-rejection does not establish equivalence. We release the partition and a five-step audit protocol that profiles shared outcomes, tests paired differences, reports grouping sensitivity, and estimates the instance budget needed for resolution. The results motivate reporting comparison-set-specific resolution and model-scaffold provenance instead of interpreting small aggregate gaps as established rank differences.
items.title: Coding Agents Have Converged: Why the SWE-bench Leaderboard Can No Longer Order Its Top Entries, and What to Measure Instead

items.summary: Agentic browsers can execute security-sensitive actions under a user's authenticated session, making indirect prompt injection and deceptive confirmation interfaces a direct threat to action integrity. Existing human-in-the-loop (HITL) safeguards are insufficient when the approval prompt itself can be influenced by untrusted page content or model-generated text. We present the \emph{Verifiable Action Card} (VAC), an architectural defence that reconstructs approval information from the ground-truth pending browser action and trusted intent provenance, renders it out-of-band in the trusted browser chrome, and binds approval to the exact action re-verified at dispatch. VAC combines provenance fencing, a ground-truth action descriptor, default-deny confirmation, provenance-aware risk gating, and execution binding. We implement VAC in a complete agentic browser and evaluate it on a 24-scenario benchmark covering confused-deputy attacks, Lies-in-the-Loop dialog forging, indirect prompt injection, adaptive action substitution, provenance evasion, and legitimate tasks. Across the evaluated LLMs, attack success without VAC ranges from $68\%$ to $100\%$, whereas VAC reduces attack success to $0\%$ on every model, with $78\%$ legitimate-task completion and a $0\%$ false-block rate. These results show that grounding approval in the action that will actually execute provides architectural protection against security failures that prompt-level defences and conventional HITL confirmation cannot reliably prevent.
items.title: The Verifiable Action Card: Trustworthy Human-in-the-Loop Control for Secure Autonomous Agents

items.summary: An advanced retrieval-augmented generation pipeline is typically assembled from three or four independently operated systems: an approximate nearest-neighbour index, a full-text search engine, a graph database, and a relational document store. Each contributes its own deployment surface, configuration model, and failure modes, and the integration logic that binds them is written anew in every project. In this work, we present \textsc{Quanta}, an open-source Python library, which unifies dense vector search over 4-bit quantised embeddings, BM25 full-text retrieval, and knowledge-graph traversal behind a single retrieval API. Quanta makes two design commitments, which distinguish it from existing hybrid retrieval stacks. First, signals are combined by \emph{weighted reciprocal rank fusion} rather than by normalising heterogeneous scores onto a shared range, which we argue is ill-posed because such normalisations are query-dependent. Second, the graph is a \emph{candidate expander and not a relevance scorer}: traversal widens the candidate pool, and the newly admitted documents are re-scored by the dense indexes under an identifier allowlist, so structural adjacency determines what is considered while content evidence determines how it ranks.
items.title: Quanta: A Self-Contained Python Library for Hybrid Retrieval over Quantised Embeddings, Lexical Indexes, and Knowledge Graphs

items.summary: Autonomous and semi-autonomous artificial intelligence systems can perform consequential work across multiple tools, repositories, services, and organizational roles. Existing governance frameworks establish valuable expectations for accountability, human oversight, risk management, logging, and provenance, but they do not collectively define an event-level control and evidence protocol for human-supervised agentic operations. This specification defines a testable profile in which a designated human supervisor retains effective operational control; every human and software actor operates under bounded authority; consequential actions pass explicit approval gates; and material events produce authenticated, append-only, independently verifiable provenance records. The profile maps organizational controls to ISO/IEC 42001:2023, ISO/IEC 38507:2022, ISO/IEC 42005:2025, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework; human oversight and logging controls to Articles 12 and 14 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; provenance semantics to W3C PROV; separation of duties to NIST SP 800-53; and cryptographic transparency to IETF RFC 9943 and RFC 9942. It also states the limits of cryptographic evidence: internal hash consistency does not establish actor identity, authorization, statement accuracy, or independent custody. HAIO-GATS is intended as a research and implementation baseline for accountable AI operations, standards development, conformity assessment, and empirical evaluation.
items.title: Human-Supervised AI Operations Governance and Audit Trail Specification: A Standards-Aligned Profile for Accountable Agentic Workflows

items.summary: This repository contains the complete synthetic dataset and reproducible code supporting the manuscript  and you need to unzip it inorder to see the files.  contents of the file include the following ;  A 2000-scenario synthetic dataset of catchment, storm, and green infrastructure (GI) typology-coverage combinations, generated from parameterized, non-linear analytical relationships (peak-flow attenuation and total-suspended-solids event-mean-concentration reduction as functions of imperviousness, storm return period, and coverage of four GI typologies: bioretention, green roofs, permeable pavement, vegetated swales). R scripts implementing the full modelling pipeline described in the manuscript: dataset generation; an 80/20 stratified train–test split; 5-fold cross-validated hyperparameter tuning; training of a linear regression baseline, a random forest model, and an XGBoost model; computation of R², RMSE, and MAE; feature-importance analysis (node-impurity for random forest, gain-based for XGBoost); and indicative runtime benchmarking. A Python implementation (scikit-learn, xgboost) used to produce the exact numbers and figures reported in the revised manuscript's Tables 1–4 and Figures 2–3, run under a fixed, documented random seed for full reproducibility. Precomputed results (model metrics, feature importances, test-set predictions) and the two main results figures as published
items.title: Machine Learning Surrogate Modelling in R for Rapid Screening of Green Infrastructure Hydrological Performance in Urban Stormwater Management: A Proof-of-Concept Study Using Synthetic Data

items.summary: SynInsight Atlas is a literature-derived synthesis pathway dataset for developing and evaluating machine-learning retrosynthesis models. It contains 6,555 reaction-step occurrences across 635 recorded paths from 91 publications , representing 2,166 distinct operations. The dataset is provided in CSV format, with molecular structures, reaction conditions, route connectivity, source references, and curation status. Field definitions, provenance records, and file checksums support reproducible reuse. This is a candidate release pending independent chemical review . Paths include partial syntheses, fragment preparations, and control branches; shared operations may occur in multiple paths. No fixed evaluation split or starting-material stock is supplied. Data and annotations are released under CC BY 4.0 . Original publications and supporting-information files are not included.
items.title: SynInsight Atlas: Literature-Derived Synthesis Pathways for Retrosynthesis Benchmarking

Benchmarks (public controlled-mixture ground truth; each bundle self-contained and self-scoring) • DDA / MaxQuant — iPRG-2015 (MassIVE RMSV000000249.2; SI Table S5a): three differential-   expression engine arms (limma, DEqMS, msqrob2) scored head-to-head against the published   MSstats reference, plus the missing-value robustness sweep (Table S7) and a reproducible   DE-runtime sweep (Table S10); and a second, independent DDA spike-in on DEqMS's own MaxLFQ   two-proteome example (PRIDE PXD000279; Table S5b). • DIA / Spectronaut — LFQbench HYE124 (Table S6a): the shipped msqrob2 default vs limma and   DEqMS arms, scored against species-defined truth and the MSstats reference; and a second,   independent DIA spike-in on the UPS1 example dataset (ExperimentHub EH7782; MassIVE   MSV000087597; Table S6b). • MSstatsPTM simulations (Table S8) and the Hogrebe two-species phospho spike-in (PRIDE   PXD007145; Table S9) — protein-adjusted PTM and site-level phospho accuracy vs MSstatsPTM,   including a native MSstatsPTM package arm. • A provenance/reports bundle (fetch scripts, checksums, and   the manuscript-cited scoring report). • Two method-validation bundles: semi-synthetic PTM-occupancy / isoform-usage mixtures (Tables   S11 and S13), and an orthogonal transcript (DM1) validation of the isoform-usage detector   (Table S12). Case studies (reproduce end-to-end from the download) • CS1 palmitate islets; CS2 FB231 mitophagy; CS3 phospho / TKI resistance (PRIDE PXD005536);   CS4 isoform-usage + PTM occupancy. Each carries its inputs, bundled annotation, recorded command   history, expected results, and sessionInfo.txt. Data availability: the benchmark inputs derive from public MassIVE/PRIDE deposits; CS3 is PRIDE PXD005536; CS1 is ethics-approved, de-identified human and stem-cell-derived islet proteomics generated by the James Johnson lab (University of British Columbia); CS2 and CS4 were generated by the Jean-François Trempe lab (McGill University).
items.title: ProteoAnalyst: benchmarks and case-study

items.summary: Agentic browsers can execute security-sensitive actions under a user's authenticated session, making indirect prompt injection and deceptive confirmation interfaces a direct threat to action integrity. Existing human-in-the-loop (HITL) safeguards are insufficient when the approval prompt itself can be influenced by untrusted page content or model-generated text. We present the \emph{Verifiable Action Card} (VAC), an architectural defence that reconstructs approval information from the ground-truth pending browser action and trusted intent provenance, renders it out-of-band in the trusted browser chrome, and binds approval to the exact action re-verified at dispatch. VAC combines provenance fencing, a ground-truth action descriptor, default-deny confirmation, provenance-aware risk gating, and execution binding. We implement VAC in a complete agentic browser and evaluate it on a 24-scenario benchmark covering confused-deputy attacks, Lies-in-the-Loop dialog forging, indirect prompt injection, adaptive action substitution, provenance evasion, and legitimate tasks. Across the evaluated LLMs, attack success without VAC ranges from $68\%$ to $100\%$, whereas VAC reduces attack success to $0\%$ on every model, with $78\%$ legitimate-task completion and a $0\%$ false-block rate. These results show that grounding approval in the action that will actually execute provides architectural protection against security failures that prompt-level defences and conventional HITL confirmation cannot reliably prevent.
items.title: The Verifiable Action Card: Trustworthy Human-in-the-Loop Control for Secure Autonomous Agents

items.summary: SynInsight Atlas is a literature-derived synthesis pathway dataset for developing and evaluating machine-learning retrosynthesis models. It contains 6,555 reaction-step occurrences across 635 recorded paths from 91 publications , representing 2,166 distinct operations. The dataset is provided in CSV format, with molecular structures, reaction conditions, route connectivity, source references, and curation status. Field definitions, provenance records, and file checksums support reproducible reuse. This is a candidate release pending independent chemical review . Paths include partial syntheses, fragment preparations, and control branches; shared operations may occur in multiple paths. No fixed evaluation split or starting-material stock is supplied. Data and annotations are released under CC BY 4.0 . Original publications and supporting-information files are not included.
items.title: SynInsight Atlas: Literature-Derived Synthesis Pathways for Retrosynthesis Benchmarking

items.summary: Autonomous and semi-autonomous artificial intelligence systems can perform consequential work across multiple tools, repositories, services, and organizational roles. Existing governance frameworks establish valuable expectations for accountability, human oversight, risk management, logging, and provenance, but they do not collectively define an event-level control and evidence protocol for human-supervised agentic operations. This specification defines a testable profile in which a designated human supervisor retains effective operational control; every human and software actor operates under bounded authority; consequential actions pass explicit approval gates; and material events produce authenticated, append-only, independently verifiable provenance records. The profile maps organizational controls to ISO/IEC 42001:2023, ISO/IEC 38507:2022, ISO/IEC 42005:2025, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework; human oversight and logging controls to Articles 12 and 14 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; provenance semantics to W3C PROV; separation of duties to NIST SP 800-53; and cryptographic transparency to IETF RFC 9943 and RFC 9942. It also states the limits of cryptographic evidence: internal hash consistency does not establish actor identity, authorization, statement accuracy, or independent custody. HAIO-GATS is intended as a research and implementation baseline for accountable AI operations, standards development, conformity assessment, and empirical evaluation.
items.title: Human-Supervised AI Operations Governance and Audit Trail Specification: A Standards-Aligned Profile for Accountable Agentic Workflows
